source_title: Integrated disposal and processing technologies for mowed roadside grass (including energetic valorisation)
publisher_or_sponsor: Bodemkundige Dienst van Belgie vzw; commissioned by OVAM
source_table_page: Table 29, printed p. 151; sampling and analysis in §§14.2.4-14.2.5, printed pp. 143-145; final-state interpretation in §14.3.2.6
license: No explicit open reuse license identified in the public report. Do not claim CC licensing; retain attribution and check reuse terms before redistribution.
geography: Ravels, Belgium; roadside grass from narrow rural roads
experiment_period: 2008 field-silo experiment; source reports sampling before ensiling, after 4 weeks, and after 10 weeks
evidence_class: B_measured_field_report; pH stability criterion is secondary literature reported in the same source

column_metadata.dry_matter_pct_fm: Reported final dry matter concentration, percent of fresh material; not a mass-retention fraction.
column_metadata.stable_silage_ph_criterion: Source-cited criterion by dry-matter level; the 4.7-4.8 entry is preserved as a range, not converted to a point.
column_metadata.storage_duration_weeks: Ten-week endpoint, cross-referenced to the source's stated final sampling period.

transcription_and_handling: Table 29 observations are transcribed into English labels. No values are imputed, no averages or loss factors are calculated, and no model default is activated. Empty DOI is intentional because no DOI was identified.
major_limitations: The silo experiment used four heterogeneous loads of roadside grass from Ravels, with variation in freshness and feed quality; the highest reported interim field storage was about three days.
Grass was cut very short by flail mower with direct suction, resulting in a high sand fraction; the roadsides had very little visible litter.

Storage mass losses cannot be quantified from this experiment because the silo mass inventory was not tracked in a micro-silo setup; final dry matter concentration is not a substitute for retained dry-matter mass.
Six treatments include co-streams and/or inoculant; they do not represent grass-only behavior or isolate one factor under fully matched feed-lot conditions.
The stated pH stability thresholds are literature criteria, not observed GreenHub control setpoints.
access_protocol: Public HTTPS PDF at the source URL; local file is a small row-level factual extract.
content_rights_note: The repository holds extracted factual observations and provenance, not the source report PDF.
